ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὅπως ἴδωσι τὰ καλὰ ἔργα ὑμῶν, καὶ δοξάσωσι τὸν
Πατέρα ὑμῶν τὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς."6 Οὐκοῦν ἐσόμεθα λαμπροὶ πε- ριφοιτώσης
ἡμᾶς καὶ οἷον ἀμφιεννύσης τῆς παρὰ Θεοῦ δόξης, οἷς ἂν χαρίσαιτο τοῖς [ἴσ. τῆς]
δικαιοσύνης ἐπιμεληταῖς· τούτων δὴ οὖν ὑπαρξάντων σοι, φησὶ, βοήσῃ τότε, καὶ ὁ
Θεὸς εἰσακούσεταί σου, ἔτι λαλοῦν- τός σου ἐρεῖ· Ἰδοὺ πάρειμι· "6Εὐχαῖς γὰρ
δικαίων ἐπ- ακούει,"6 κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον. Καὶ καθά φησιν ὁ Μελῳδὸς,
"6Ὀφθαλμοὶ Κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους, καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ εἰς δέησιν αὐτῶν."6 Κατανεύσει
μὲν γὰρ τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν ὡς ἀγαθὸς, ἀλλ' οὐχ ἅπασι παραχρῆμα. Τοῖς γε μὴν
διαπρέψασιν ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, μελλησμοῦ δίχα παντὸς ὀρέγει τὰ αἰτήματα, καὶ
ἑτοιμοτάτην αὐτοῖς ὑπέχει τὴν ἀκοὴν, ὥστε καὶ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν αἰτημάτων
χαίροντας λέγειν· "6Ἤκουσεν ἐκ ναοῦ ἁγίου αὐτοῦ φωνῆς μου, καὶ ἡ κραυγή μου
ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ."6 Οὐκοῦν τὸ ἀνυπέρθετον τῆς
φιλοτιμίας, καὶ τὸ λίαν ἕτοιμον τοῦ διδόντος Θεοῦ παρίστησιν ἐναργῶς τὸ, Ἰδοὺ
πάρειμι, βοᾷν, ἔτι λαλοῦντος δικαίου, ἀνατείνοντός τε τὰς λιτάς. 9Ἐὰν ἀφέλῃς
ἀπὸ σοῦ σύνδεσμον, καὶ χειροτο- νίαν, καὶ ῥῆμα γογγυσμοῦ, καὶ δῷς πεινῶντι τὸν
ἄρτον σου, καὶ ψυχὴν τεταπεινωμένην ἐμ- πλήσῃς, τότε ἀνατελεῖ ἐν τῷ σκότει τὸ
φῶς σου, καὶ τὸ σκότος σου ἐν μεσημβρίᾳ, καὶ ἔσται ὁ Θεός σου μετὰ σοῦ
διαπαντός.9 Τὰ τῶν μαθημάτων ἐξαίρετα κἂν πολλάκις λέγηταί τισιν, ἀλλ' οὖν
ἔχει τὸ ὀνησιφόρον. Γράφει γοῦν ὁ πάνσοφος Παῦλος τοῖς δι' αὐτοῦ πιστεύσασι·
"6Τὰ αὐτὰ λέγειν ὑμῖν, ἐμοὶ μὲν οὐκ ὀκνηρὸν, ὑμῖν δὲ ἀσφαλές."6 Οὐκοῦν
πολυτρόπως διὰ τῶν αὐτῶν ἡμῖν ἔρχεται λέ- γων καὶ τὰς τῆς εὐδοκιμήσεως ὁδοὺς
ἐναργεῖς καθ- ιστὰς, καὶ τῶν δοθησομένων τοῖς ἁγίοις γερῶν τὴν φαιδρότητα
διηγούμενος, ἵνα καὶ ἔτι μειζόνως προ- θυμοτέρους ἐργάσηται πρὸς τὸ ἑλέσθαι δρᾷν
τὰ δι' ὧν ἂν γένοιντο σεπτοὶ, καὶ τὴν ἄνωθεν καὶ παρ' αὐτοῦ 70.1292 φιλοτιμίαν
εὑρήσουσιν. Οὐκοῦν, "6Ἐὰν ἀφέλης, φη- σὶν, ἀπὸ σοῦ σύνδεσμον, καὶ χειροτονίαν."6
Καὶ σύνδεσμον μὲν, ὥς γε οἶμαι, φησὶ τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν μοχθηρίαν, σκαιότητά τε καὶ
τὸ φιλόνεικον, καὶ τὸ οἷον συνδέσμους πραγμάτων ἐργάζεσθαι κατά τινων, καὶ
σκολιῶν εὑρεμάτων ποιεῖσθαι ζητήσεις, ὡς κατα- δεσμεῖν ἔσθ' ὅτε τινὰς, καὶ
ἀφύκτοις περιστάσεων ἐνιέναι βρόχοις. ∆εῖ γὰρ ἁπλοῦν, καὶ εὐπρόσιτον εἶναι τὸν
ἄνθρωπον, εἴπερ ἔχοι σκοπὸν ἐφορᾶσθαι παρὰ Θεοῦ, καὶ τῶν παρ' αὐτοῦ γλίχεσθαι
χαρισμάτων. Χειροτονίαν δὲ τάχα πού φησι τὴν δωροδοκίαν, καὶ τὸ λημμάτων
αἰσχρῶν ἐφίεσθαι, φαμὲν γὰρ ἔσθ' ὅτε
pass_a_gloss: [...] [brightness] benefits not moderately those who look upon them. And indeed Christ said to the holy apostles: Let your light shine before men, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in the heavens. So we will be bright, the glory from God going around us and as it were clothing [us], which he would grant to those who devote themselves to the [another reading: of the] righteousness; these then having been present to you, he says, you will cry then, and God will listen to you, while you are still speaking he will say: Behold, I am present. For he listens to prayers of righteous, according to what is written. And as the Melodist says: Eyes of the Lord upon righteous, and his ears to their petition. For he will assent to those asking as good, but not to all immediately. But to those distinguished in righteousness, without any delay he holds out the requests, and holds under them a most ready hearing, so that also over each of the requests, rejoicing, they say: He heard from his holy temple my voice, and my cry before him will enter into his ears. So the unpostponed [nature] of the generosity, and the very great readiness of the God who gives, the 'Behold, I am present' sets forth clearly, crying while the righteous is still speaking and raising the supplications. [Lemma, Isaiah 58:9-11:] If you take away from you a bond, and a stretching out of hand, and a word of grumbling, and give your bread to the hungry, and fill a humbled soul, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness at noon, and your God will be with you always. The choice things of the lessons, even if often said to some, yet have the beneficial. So the all-wise Paul writes to those who believed through him: To say the same things to you is not troublesome to me, and safe for you. So in many ways through the same things he comes to us, saying and making clear the ways of good repute, and narrating the brightness of the gifts that will be given to the saints, so that also still more greatly he might make them more eager toward choosing to do the things through which they might become revered, and will find the generosity from above and from him. So, If you take away, he says, from you a bond and a stretching out of hand. And bond, as I think, he says the wickedness of the nations [read: of character], and perversity and love of quarrel, and as it were working bonds of affairs against some, and making searches of crooked inventions, so as sometimes to bind some down, and to put them into inescapable nooses of troubles. For man must be simple and easy of approach, if he should have the aim to be watched over by God, and to long for the gifts from him. And stretching out of hand he perhaps says the taking of bribes, and the reaching after shameful gains; for we say sometimes [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … brightness benefits in no small measure those who look on them. Indeed, Christ said to the holy apostles: “Let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven” (Matthew 5:16). So we shall be radiant, with the glory from God moving all around us and, as it were, clothing us, the glory he would grant to those who devote themselves to righteousness.

When these things are yours, he says, then you will cry out, and God will hear you; while you are still speaking he will say, “Here I am” (Isaiah 58:9). For “he listens to the prayers of the righteous” (Proverbs 15:29), as it is written. And as the Psalmist says: “The eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer” (Psalm 34:15).

Because he is good, he will grant the requests of those who ask, but not to all at once. To those who have excelled in righteousness, however, he holds out what they ask without any delay and lends them a most ready ear, so that over each of their requests they say with joy: “He heard my voice from his holy temple, and my cry before him will come into his ears” (Psalm 18:6). So the cry “Here I am,” while the righteous man is still speaking and lifting up his prayers, shows plainly the generosity that will not delay and the great readiness of God who gives.

“If you take away from yourself the bond, and the stretching out of the hand, and the word of grumbling, and give your bread to the hungry, and satisfy the humbled soul, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your darkness will be as noon, and your God will be with you always” (Isaiah 58:9–11).

The choicest lessons, even if people hear them many times, still bring benefit. So the all-wise Paul writes to those who believed through him: “To say the same things to you is no trouble to me, and for you it is safe” (Philippians 3:1). So in many ways he comes to us saying the same things, making plain the roads to good standing and describing the splendor of the rewards to be given to the saints. He does this to make them still more eager to choose to do the things by which they would become worthy of honor and would find the generosity that comes from above, from him.

So he says, “If you take away from yourself the bond, and the stretching out of the hand” (Isaiah 58:9). By “bond,” I think, he means wickedness of character, perversity and love of quarrels, and, as it were, tying knots of trouble against people and searching out crooked schemes, so as at times to bind people fast and throw them into snares of hardship from which there is no escape.

choices.why: Septuagint Isaiah 58:9; Cyril reads it as the hand held out for bribes.
